name: Schenley Overlook circuit
description: A climb to the overlook, a pass by the Oval, and a return through Schenley Park.

destination.name: Schenley Dr & Schenley Dr Ext · route start

terrain: Mostly paved park roads and shared paths, with climbing and descents. Mixed traffic at road connections; walk short station access paths where bicycle access is unclear.
bikeAdvice: An e-bike can help with the climb. Pedal bikes suit riders comfortable with hills.
rentalNote: Allow extra time for the climb, crossings, and stops. A moving-time estimate does not guarantee a ride under your membership allowance.
cautions: Follow the plotted direction on the one-way part of Overlook Drive.
Use marked road crossings and yield on shared paths. This is not an entirely traffic-free ride.
The approach from TCS Hall is not included. Start and finish at station 33.
overview: Start at Schenley Dr & Schenley Dr Ext.
Follow the mapped Schenley/Panther Hollow connection to climb Overlook Drive.
Pass the overlook and Oval; return via the eastern park-road connection and the mapped shared path.
Finish at station 33; confirm an open dock before returning.

name: Eliza Furnace out-and-back
description: Follow the Eliza Furnace Trail toward downtown, then retrace it to the Swinburne trailhead.

destination.name: Eliza Furnace Trail & Swineburne St · route start

terrain: Paved shared-use trail with a relatively gentle elevation profile. The turnaround stays on the trail before the downtown street connection.
bikeAdvice: Either bike type suits the trail. An e-bike is optional; it does not extend your included rental time.
rentalNote: The full out-and-back may exceed 30 minutes. A shorter outing needs an earlier turnaround and a buffer for docking; no fixed turnaround guarantees a free ride.
cautions: Slow for trail users, gates, and the turnaround.
The campus descent and return climb are excluded. Start and finish at trail-side station 2.
Station 49 is a nearby reference with an access detour; it is not a guaranteed mid-ride rental reset.
overview: Start at the Eliza Furnace trailhead by station 2.
Follow the plotted trail toward downtown.
Turn around at the marked point before the downtown street connection, or earlier for a shorter outing.
Retrace the trail and finish at station 2.

name: Monongahela river loop
description: A longer circuit using Eliza Furnace, Smithfield Street Bridge, the South Side, and Hot Metal Bridge.

destination.name: Technology Dr & Bates St · route start

terrain: Mostly shared-use trails with bridge ramps, short street connectors, and a small fine-gravel section. The Station Square/South Side connection includes busy-road riding and a railway crossing.
bikeAdvice: Either bike type can work. Choose this ride only if comfortable with the plotted street connectors; an e-bike can ease the longer outing.
rentalNote: The full loop exceeds 30 minutes at the assumed 12–18 km/h. Check membership costs, or plan separate rentals only when bikes and docks are actually available. Nearby stations do not guarantee a free reset.
cautions: Walk short station access paths and use marked crossings at Second Avenue and bridge approaches.
The Station Square connector uses streets, including part of East Carson Street. This is not a continuous protected trail.
Cross railway tracks at the marked crossing near S 4th Street; never enter a closed crossing.
Check current trail notices. The campus connection is excluded; start and finish at station 49.
overview: Start at station 49 and use the plotted crossing to reach Eliza Furnace Trail.
Ride toward downtown and follow the mapped connection onto Smithfield Street Bridge.
Use the Station Square/South Side street connector, then join South Side Trail near S 4th Street.
Follow the trail upstream, cross the bicycle side of Hot Metal Bridge, and return to station 49.

description: A shorter Eliza Furnace out-and-back for an easy weekday ride.
terrain: Mostly paved shared trail with a gentle grade. The approach from CMU is separate.
quickNote: Short paved trail ride. Leave time to dock.
cautions: Stay on the shared trail and yield to people walking.
Turn at the plotted point; this shorter ride does not reach downtown.
Campus travel is excluded. Start and finish at station 2.
overview: Start at station 2 by the Swinburne trailhead.
Follow Eliza Furnace Trail west to the plotted turnaround.
Retrace the trail and return to station 2.
bikeAdvice: Either bike suits the mostly flat trail. Choose an e-bike if you want help reaching the start.
rentalNote: Moving time excludes stops and travel to the start. Leave time for an available dock; this estimate is not a rental allowance.

name: South Side riverside
description: A short, mostly flat ride along the South Side riverfront trail.
terrain: Mostly paved riverside shared trail. Use the trail-side dock at S 4th Street; no approach from East Carson Street is included.
quickNote: Mostly flat shared trail. Start at the trail-side dock.
cautions: Yield to people walking, especially near the park and boat access.
Start on the trail side of the railway at station 9. Access from elsewhere in South Side may involve the railway crossing.
Campus travel is excluded; check dock availability before returning to station 9.
overview: Start at station 9 on the South Side Trail.
Follow the riverside trail east toward South Side Riverfront Park.
Turn at the plotted point and retrace the trail to station 9.

name: North Shore riverfront
description: An easy riverside out-and-back past PNC Park along the Allegheny.
terrain: Mostly paved riverfront shared trail with short ramps and underpasses. This starts on the North Shore, farther from CMU.
quickNote: Riverfront trail with busy shared areas near PNC Park.
cautions: Slow down near pedestrians, underpasses, and stadium crowds; follow event closures.
Stay on the north bank. This avoids the Convention Center bank and does not head west to Chateau.
Campus travel is excluded. Start and finish at station 23.
overview: Start at station 23 near Fort Duquesne Bridge.
Follow the riverfront trail east past PNC Park, staying on the north bank.
Turn near Rachel Carson Bridge and retrace the track to station 23.
bikeAdvice: Either bike suits the mostly flat trail. Choose an e-bike if you want help reaching the start.
rentalNote: Moving time excludes stops and travel to the start. Leave time for an available dock; this estimate is not a rental allowance.

name: Junction Hollow greenway
description: A greenway out-and-back along the western edge of Schenley Park.
terrain: Paved shared trail with a gentle climb, using the marked connection from the Eliza Furnace trailhead. Turn before the Boundary Street road section.
bikeAdvice: Either bike works; an e-bike can help on the gradual return grades.
quickNote: Stay on the marked trail; do not cross the railway toward the lake.
overview: Start at station 2 by the Swinburne trailhead.
Follow the plotted connection to Junction Hollow Trail.
Turn before Boundary Street and retrace the route to station 2.
cautions: Yield to walkers and use the marked crossings on the trail connection.
Do not use informal railway crossings toward Panther Hollow Lake.
The route does not include travel from CMU or the steep streets north of the trail.
rentalNote: Allow extra time for stops, crossings, and an available dock. Moving time excludes travel from CMU and does not guarantee the membership time allowance.

name: North Shore stadium trail
description: Head west along the waterfront toward the stadium and science center.
terrain: Paved riverside shared paths and promenade. The turnaround stays on the bicycle-permitted trail by the science center.
bikeAdvice: Either bike suits this short riverside ride.
quickNote: Shared promenade: slow down for crowds and event closures.
overview: Start at station 23 near Fort Duquesne Bridge.
Follow the North Shore waterfront west toward the stadium and science center.
Turn at the plotted trail point and return to station 23.
cautions: Pedestrians and stadium-event crowds may require dismounting.
This route turns well before the Chateau repair closure; current signs still take precedence.
Travel from CMU is excluded; check an open dock before returning.
rentalNote: Allow extra time for stops, crossings, and an available dock. Moving time excludes travel from CMU and does not guarantee the membership time allowance.

name: Hot Metal & GAP ride
description: Cross the bicycle bridge, then follow the GAP toward Hays and back.
terrain: Bicycle bridge ramps and mostly paved shared trail, with short dock-access paths. Allow extra time and effort for the ramps.
bikeAdvice: An e-bike can help on the bridge ramps. Pedal bikes suit riders comfortable with the ramps.
quickNote: Use the bicycle bridge; walk the short dock-access paths.
overview: Start at station 49, Technology Dr & Bates St.
Follow the plotted connection across the bicycle side of Hot Metal Bridge.
Follow the GAP south to the plotted turnaround, then return over the same bridge to station 49.
cautions: Walk the short station access where bicycle access is unclear, and use marked crossings.
Stay on the bicycle bridge; the road bridge is a separate crossing.
There are no guaranteed docks at the turnaround. Keep a buffer for the return rental and docking.
This short ride does not reach the Duquesne–Homestead closure; do not extend through a signed closure.
rentalNote: Allow extra time for stops, crossings, and an available dock. Moving time excludes travel from CMU and does not guarantee the membership time allowance.

name: Hazelwood Trail out-and-back
description: Ride toward Hazelwood Green on the riverfront trail and retrace it.
terrain: Mostly paved shared trail with fine-gravel connecting sections near the north end. The turnaround is on the trail before the street crossing into Hazelwood Green.
bikeAdvice: Either bike can use the shared trail. Slow down on fine gravel and avoid riding through construction.
quickNote: Fine-gravel sections; stay on the marked public trail.
overview: Start at station 2 by the Eliza Furnace trailhead.
Use the plotted trail connection toward Hazelwood, staying on the north bank.
Turn before the Hazelwood Green street crossing and retrace the track to station 2.
cautions: Slow down on fine gravel, especially after rain.
Hazelwood Green is an evolving construction site; follow signs and stay in designated public areas.
The route excludes campus travel and does not use the one-way bike lanes farther into the site.
rentalNote: Allow extra time for stops, crossings, and an available dock. Moving time excludes travel from CMU and does not guarantee the membership time allowance.
